source_read: Saved PubMed Central page text (PMC6890973), read in full: abstract, Research in context, sections 1–5, Tables 1–2 (as text), CRediT statement, acknowledgements, disclosures and funding; reference list checked for the cited studies. Figures 1–3 are images; the supplements were not available.

anchors.note: Unadjusted; level of evidence C; weighted quality 77%. The seven studies' Ns in Table 1 sum to 3469 (McKetin 2013 counted as 1064 observation-months from 278 people), not the printed 3436.

anchors.locator: Results › 3.1 Characteristics of included studies, 2nd paragraph (quality 68%; confounding shortfall) and the paragraph after Table 1 (too few studies for funnel plots); Discussion › 4.1 Limitations of the evidence, 1st paragraph
anchors.note: Data right: average quality 68% of applicable Joanna Briggs checklist items across the 59 meta-analysed studies (64% for all 149); the commonest shortfall was failure to identify and control for confounders. That publication bias could not be examined is stated after Table 1 and in 4.1, not at the stated place. For the psychosis pools specifically, Table 2 gives weighted quality of 77% (any use) and 75% (use disorder), unadjusted.

for_senior_author: AMSTAR 2 (the one risk-of-bias change, at the coordinator's request): items 6, 11, 12 and 14 carried 'partial yes', which AMSTAR 2 does not offer for them; re-decided from the text as yes (6), yes (11), no (12) and yes (14), each logged on the card. Overall recomputed with the critical-item rule: items 7 and 15 are 'no', so critically low stands (reader 2 also agreed with critically low). Two points to check: item 11 is a close call (crude 2×2 data pooled as the headline unadjusted estimates, adjusted estimates pooled separately); and if the unread supplement holds the excluded-studies list (item 7), item 15 would be the only critical flaw and the rating would become low, unless item 11 is judged 'no'.
not_added: Any-use psychosis n: Table 2 prints 3436 while the seven studies' Ns in Table 1 sum to 3469: confirmed; a 33-participant discrepancy, noted on anchor 0 of cl_meth_psychosis_association.
Section 3.6 calls five of the seven any-use depression studies 'half' of the included studies: the referent is unclear; not added.
